subject: Marketplace reseller addendum — billing & invoice ownership
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@nimbuscloud.com>, Tom Keller <t.keller@nimbuscloud.com>
Cc: marketplace-ops@nimbuscloud.com
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Marketplace reseller addendum — billing & invoice ownership

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks for taking the time on the call yesterday. As we discussed, the Nimbus marketplace onboarding team sent over a draft reseller addendum (attached) but we need to align on the billing & invoice ownership flow before we can sign. A few specific asks from our side: 

- Confirm which party issues the customer-facing invoice when a sale occurs through the Nimbus marketplace (Marketplace invoice vs. Reseller invoice).
- How taxes/VAT/withholding are handled and which party is contractually responsible for remitting them.
- Audit/fraud reconciliation: who owns payment reconciliation and chargeback investigations?
- Data retention and reporting cadence — we prefer daily usage exports for revenue traceability.

I've attached a redlines summary (redlines_summary_camila.pdf) with inline notes that reflect Redwood's preferred positions. High-level proposal: Nimbus invoices the end customer, Nimbus remits payment to Redwood with a single monthly settlement, and Redwood retains audit rights with 90 days' notice. We are open to a mutually agreeable compromise on tax language and liability caps — if Nimbus insists on bearing invoicing responsibility, we need a clear indemnity and an SLA for reconciliations.

Can you flag the sections in your next pass where you cannot accept the proposed language, and we will route to legal for counter-redlines. If helpful, I'm available for a 30-minute sync Monday morning PT.

Thanks,

Camila Reyes
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Nimbus_Marketplace_Addendum_v3.docx, redlines_summary_camila.pdf
From: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@nimbuscloud.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 14:30:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace reseller addendum — billing & invoice ownership

Camila —

Thanks for the clear note and the redlines. Quick summary of our stance:

- Nimbus prefers marketplace-issued invoices to keep payment flow consolidated through our billing platform.
- Nimbus will handle tax collection for marketplace transactions in jurisdictions where we are the seller of record, but we expect Redwood to provide timely tax residency information and any resale certificates where applicable.
- For settlement, Nimbus proposes a biweekly remittance to Redwood with a 15-day reconciliation window.
- Regarding audits, we can provide usage reports and a reconciliation API; we generally resist unilateral audit rights that allow on-site reviews.

I've attached our annotated draft with inline comments and one alternative paragraph for indemnity that limits our exposure but adds a shared investigation clause. We flagged the invoice ownership, settlement cadence, and audit language as must-discuss items.

Would Monday 9:00 PT work for a short call to converge?

Best,

Elena Ortiz
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
NimbusCloud
elena.ortiz@nimbuscloud.com

Subject: Re: Marketplace reseller addendum — billing & invoice ownership

Elena —

Monday 9:00 PT works — thanks. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Karthik (channel) so we can triage the redlines live. A few prep notes for legal context so we make the call efficient: 

- If Nimbus is the invoice owner, Redwood needs a clause that (a) guarantees remittance timing (biweekly OK but prefer monthly with net-15), (b) requires an escrow or short dispute resolution mechanism for chargebacks, and (c) includes a clear reconciliation SLA (48–72 hours for discrepant items).
- For taxes: we can provide resale certificates where applicable, but we can't accept blanket tax indemnities for actions outside of our control — propose a carveout for taxes that arise from Nimbus's invoicing model.
- Audit: our preference is documented API access and daily exports; on-site audits require at least 30 days' prior notice and scope limitation.

Please find attached a one-page redline summary that distills our top five non-negotiables. We'll aim to resolve settlement cadence and invoice ownership on the call.

Thanks,

Camila

Elena / Camila / team —

Thanks for looping me in. I reviewed the back-and-forth and have proposed compromise language inline (attached) but wanted to call out the legal tradeoffs so the commercial team can weigh in before the call: 

1) Invoice owner model: If Nimbus issues invoices, we must get (i) a representation that Nimbus is the seller of record in those jurisdictions, (ii) express indemnity limited to third-party tax liabilities arising from Nimbus's billing errors, and (iii) a 12-month lookback right to reconcile revenue. Redwood cannot accept open-ended responsibility for tax shortfalls originating from Nimbus's invoicing.

2) Settlement frequency: Biweekly remittances add operational overhead and FX exposure; we prefer monthly net-15 with a short window for accelerated payout if volumes exceed a threshold. If Nimbus requires biweekly, include a fee offset clause for increased transaction costs.

3) Audit & data access: API/reporting-first approach is fine. Add a clause restricting type and scope of data (no PII export without a DPA amendment) and require 30-day notice for any manual or on-site review. Any findings that materially reduce Redwood's revenue should trigger an escalation path and temporary withholding caps.

4) Disputes & chargebacks: Add a 60-day cure period for disputed settlements and require Nimbus to put disputed funds into escrow while investigations proceed.

I've attached "Marissa_Redlines_Nimbus.docx" with exact redline text. Camila/Karthik — if commercial is prepared to accept limited indemnities and a monthly cadence with an FX fee offset, we can approve the invoice-owner model. Otherwise, we should push for Nimbus to remain the payer and Redwood to invoice customers directly in key regions (US/EU).

We can review live on the call; please confirm the calendar invite for Mon 9:00 PT (I should be on mute from 9:30–10:00 but will attend).

Regards,
